title: GEO: Generative Engine Optimization
summary: Foundational paper (KDD 2024) that defines generative engine optimization and the GEO-bench benchmark of queries with web sources. The authors report that content-level strategies can raise visibility in generative engine responses by up to 40%, with effects that vary by domain. A 2026 survey (also in this log) argues the gains hold only when a source is already in the engine context.

title: A new resource for optimizing for generative AI in Google Search
summary: Google Search Central (John Mueller) announces its guide to optimizing for generative AI features, stressing unique high-value content and that standard SEO remains central. The guide addresses AEO and GEO misconceptions, local, shopping, image and video content, and gives early guidance on AI agents.

title: Optimizing your website for generative AI features on Google Search
summary: Official Google guide: generative AI features rest on core ranking and quality systems, Google does not treat AEO or GEO as separate disciplines, and mass-producing pages for query variations counts as scaled content abuse. It states that llms.txt, special markup, content chunking, rewriting for AI and manufactured mentions are not needed or helpful, and points to the Generative AI performance report for measurement. Publication month taken from the announcement post; the page shows no date.

title: AI features and your website (Google Search Central)
summary: Official documentation on AI Overviews and AI Mode: a page needs only to be indexed and snippet-eligible, with no extra requirements or special markup. Both features may use query fan-out, issuing several related searches, so they can show a wider set of links than classic Search, and the two may use different models. Controls are robots.txt, nosnippet, data-nosnippet, max-snippet and noindex; AI traffic is counted in the Web search type of Search Console. Year of first publication is approximate: the page exposes no date.

title: Introducing Search Generative AI performance reports in Search Console
summary: Search Console gains reports showing impressions of a site URLs in AI Overviews, AI Mode and Discover generative features, by page, country, device (Search only) and date. Impressions are the only metric so far; the page notes rollout to all websites worldwide as of 31 August 2026. Clicks from these features remain inside the overall performance report.

title: Supporting a shared AI training control for websites
summary: Google announces support for a shared robots.txt policy token for AI training preferences, based on the draft IETF AIPREF work. A training opt-out via the token is treated as a Google-Extended disallow when Google-Extended is not mentioned, and sites that explicitly allow Google-Extended can be eligible for Gemini Apps grounding responses and clicks. Google targets support in 2027; the proposal is still a draft.

title: New Research: Traffic to the Open Web Has Fallen 12% in 5 Years; Visits per Web User Are Down 30%
summary: Similarweb panel data show worldwide browser visits at about 1.97 trillion in Q3 2026, 12.2% below the Q1 2022 peak, while web users grew about 24% and visits per user fell about 29%. The data cover browser traffic only (no apps), do not quantify the share caused by AI tools, and the top 100 sites gained only about 3% share.

title: We Analyzed 118,000 ChatGPT Prompts from 12,000+ Users: How Do Americans Use AI Tools in 2026?
summary: Opt-in Verso panel of 12,321 US ChatGPT users (118,163 prompts, January to October 2026). 12.1% of responses included a brand and 6.9% of prompts involved researching a brand to buy from; shopping, brands and local services were 5.7% of conversations. The author concludes ChatGPT is mostly an assistant rather than a search substitute; the panel skews young and female and excludes API use.

title: Is AI Visibility a Marketing Boondoggle?
summary: Rand Fishkin argues AI visibility should not absorb most marketing effort or budget and should be treated as a brand channel, not a traffic channel. He cites Marie Haynes (100 sites: all LLMs 0.73% of traffic, Google 97% of conversions), SEOWorks UK (95 sites: organic sent about 39 times more traffic than AI assistants) and a Growth Memo test that found no reliable link between AI visibility and branded or direct traffic.

title: AI Search Meta Analysis - Q4 2026
summary: Kevin Indig reviews 32 of 52 studies without pooling them. Click losses with AI answers range from about 5% (Wikipedia referrals) to about 40-58% depending on design (Pew 8% vs 15% click rate; Ahrefs position-one CTR 1.6% vs 3.7%), while a Semrush/Datos analysis found a slight zero-click drop. In an AirOps study 85% of retrieved pages were never cited and 32.9% of cited top-20 pages appeared only for fan-out queries; many samples are small and several authors sell AI search products.

title: How software buyers use AI
summary: Survey of 200 software-buyer experiences (with Wynter; the author discloses an investment in Wynter): AI chats added a new vendor to the shortlist for 62.7% of 158 respondents who already had vendors in mind, 72.5% visited vendor sites afterwards and 48% searched Google. Of 126 who chose a vendor, 78 said it appeared in the first AI answer; an AI mention does not guarantee a demo or purchase. B2B-specific and self-reported.

title: Which Types of Mentions Correlate the Strongest With AI Visibility? (260M AI Prompts Analyzed)
summary: Ahrefs (vendor) correlates seven off-site mention types with AI mentions for 10,000 US brands across 260M non-branded prompts in AI Overviews, AI Mode and ChatGPT. Reddit ranking-thread mentions correlate strongest (0.75), then domain and webpage mentions (0.70), news (0.67), YouTube (0.64) and TikTok (0.60); ChatGPT shows the weakest link. Correlation only: brand size explains part of it, and within search-volume bands correlations drop to 0.34-0.54.

title: Where Does ChatGPT Get Its Information? 4 Sources, Explained
summary: Ahrefs (vendor) describes four inputs to ChatGPT answers: training data, live web search with fan-out, licensed publisher content and user context. By its own studies, 83% of brand-question answers cited the brand site, only about 8% of citations ranked in the Google or Bing top 10, about a quarter of cited pages repeated the next day, and schema produced no significant change. Mostly single-vendor data and single-person tests.

title: Google AI Overviews cite self-serving listicles but recommend competitors
summary: Lily Ray analysed 100 B2B best-category queries in AI Overviews at three dates between April and June 2026, using Ahrefs Brand Radar data. A brand own self-promotional listicle was cited but the brand was left out of the recommendation in about 69% of cases; Google leaned on third-party and user-generated sources, with Reddit citations rising. Details come from secondary coverage because the article returned HTTP 403; exact date not confirmed.

title: Optimizing Visibility in Generative Engines: A Critical Survey of Generative Engine Optimization (2023-2026)
summary: Single-author survey of 45 GEO studies, arguing the original GEO gains hold only when a source is already in a fixed context and so do not show organic discoverability. Topical relevance and context position are the most reproducible levers, generic heuristics transfer poorly, citation-oriented rewrites can impair retrieval, and commercial audits show low overlap across engines and high run-to-run variability. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

title: Generative Engine Optimization at Scale: Measuring Brand Visibility Across AI Search Engines
summary: Preprint by a vendor author (Ranqo) analysing 100,000+ responses on 100+ brands in ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity and Gemini, March to May 2026. Global brands appeared in 73% of relevant answers, mid-market brands in 44% and niche brands in 11%; about 78% of citations went to corporate sites and ranked listicles were the top format (about 21%). Sentiment framing changed about 6.7 times more often than mention presence. Vendor-linked, not peer reviewed.

title: GEO-Bench: Benchmarking Ranking Manipulation in Generative Engine Optimization
summary: Benchmark comparing black-box, white-box and white-hat ranking-manipulation methods on five datasets against a fixed open-weight ranker (Llama-3.1-8B). Black-box rewriting matched or beat gradient attacks and in some domains evaded keyword and perplexity detectors, and attacker access did not predict strength. Evidence comes from a small open model, so it matters mainly for understanding manipulation risk.

title: The half-life of an AI citation is 11 days
summary: Profound (vendor selling citation-decay tracking) followed 883,000 cited pages across seven engines over 12 months. The median page lost half its peak citation share 11 days after peaking and 78% decayed within two weeks. Pages cited by five or more engines were about 5.5 times as likely to persist at eight weeks, Claude retained citations longest, and news or research-report pages decayed fastest.

title: Building the AI platform for marketing (Series D)
summary: Profound announced a Series D of 180 million USD at a 1.8 billion USD valuation, led by Sequoia Capital and Kleiner Perkins, with existing investors participating (company announcement, September 2026). It is the largest disclosed round among pure-play AI visibility vendors found in this run.

title: ChatGPT Business Hub: what the numbers tell you
summary: Peec AI (vendor) reviews OpenAI new Business Hub, part of Businesses in ChatGPT (beta, 10 November 2026). It reports mentions (links and citations to the site; unlinked brand mentions excluded), clicks and CTR (below 1% for nearly every brand checked) and top discovery topics over 7 or 28 days, but not prompts, fan-out queries, competitors or recommendations.

title: Introducing Businesses in ChatGPT
summary: OpenAI launched Businesses in ChatGPT in beta on 10 November 2026; per Peec AI, claiming a business gives access to a Business Hub with first-party reporting on ChatGPT references, clicks and discovery topics. This summary rests on the secondary review because the OpenAI page returned HTTP 403.

title: AI Overviews have nearly doubled across five commercial search modifiers
summary: Semrush (vendor) reports AI Overviews on 88% of tracked US commercial keywords with modifiers such as reviews, pricing and comparisons, up from about 46% a year earlier. The sample is limited (400 desktop keywords in banking, ecommerce and software, per Growth Memo), so it should not be read as a share of all queries.
